title: Test quality review
summary: Judge whether a change's tests prove behavior rather than existence: trivial assertions, mocked-away boundaries and untested failure paths are findings.

provenance.notes: Encodes this project's rule that a passing test must demonstrate a behavior, not the existence of a definition.

inputs.name: criteria
inputs.description: Acceptance criteria the tests should prove.

outputs.name: gaps
outputs.description: Behaviors or failure paths with no meaningful test.

outputs.name: weak-tests
outputs.description: Tests that cannot fail, with the reason.

workflow.step: Map each acceptance criterion and each changed branch to a test; list the ones with none.
workflow.check: The map names test functions you read.

workflow.step: For each test ask what change to the implementation would make it fail; if none, it is weak.
workflow.check: Tests that assert only length, presence or a static name are flagged.

workflow.step: Find mocks that replace the exact boundary being tested and tests that restate the implementation.
workflow.check: The mocked boundary is not the thing under test.

workflow.step: Look for missing negative, boundary, concurrency and cancellation cases.
workflow.check: At least the documented failure modes have a test.

workflow.step: Rank gaps by the risk of the untested behavior and propose the single most valuable test to add.

constraints: Read-only: propose tests, do not write or run them.
Do not count line coverage as evidence of behavior coverage.
A flaky test is a finding, not something to retry until green.

examples.title: Existence test
examples.situation: A test asserts the agent list has 16 entries.
examples.guidance: Flag it as weak: it passes if every agent is broken. Propose a test that executes one agent through its workflow with a scripted model.

verification: Each finding names a test or a missing test and the behavior at risk.
Weak tests are justified by the mutation that would not fail them.

task.text: Review the test quality: weak test assertions and untested failure paths.
Evaluate whether the mocked boundary makes the test coverage meaningless; add a negative test.
